structure: Part 5, Add an address. Read in full: the address-type step (address-type/page.js, address-type.controller.js, address-type.njk), the add page (add/page.js, add.controller.js, add.njk), the shared address-fields.njk macro, fields.js (field rules), field-rule.js, address-countries.js, add-in-progress.js (the session store for an add in progress), stored-address.js, lines-html.js, the address-book copy in English and Welsh (copy.en.js, copy.cy.js; only the add, addressType, form, roles, add success banner and field error keys claimed here), lib/validate (index.js, run.js, validators.js, calendar.js), the countries service (client.js, index.js, stub.js), and the fit helper address-form.js with the two fit specs add.fit.spec.js and address-type.fit.spec.js. Also looked up, for routes and roles only: shared/paths.js (address-book, add and address-type paths and the start query) and services/address-book/address-types.js (address types, form types, roles by type, place roles), and the ROLES_BY_PARTY table in common/test-helpers/journey-handshake.js. Covered: two pages. The address-type page at /address-book/add/address-type (three radio options with hints, one error, Continue, Back, where each option leads, the start query that clears an add in progress). The add page at /address-book/add in its two modes: the address-book mode (after the address-type step, roles question by address type, Save and continue, Cancel and return to address book, success banner and landing on the type's list tab) and the role-handshake mode a notification journey opens (journey strip, the other-roles question, Save and select, Save and return to address page, Cancel and return to hub). For both: every address and contact field with label, hint, width, autocomplete, required and maximum length, the country select and how its list is built from reference data, every validation message in English and Welsh, error handling when the address book refuses or fails, and what is saved. Every validator exported by lib/validate with its limits, and which ones the address fields use. Every test in the two fit specs, a looped test claimed once naming its instances. The handshake context, return URL and journey registry mechanics themselves are part 3's; the list the add lands on is part 4's; view, edit and delete are part 6's.

claims.statement: The address-type page is served at GET and POST /address-book/add/address-type.
The address-type page is marked at maturity 'exploring'.
A user reaches the address-type page from the address book list's 'Add a new address' button, which links to the address-type page with the query start=true.
Opening the address-type page with start=true clears any address being added (the chosen type, the entered values and the ticked roles), so a new add starts with nothing chosen.
claims.note: mechanism: clears the session record of the add in progress. The clearing is logged with the organisation id and path.

claims.statement: The address-type page shows the caption 'Add a new address'.
The address-type page's heading and page title are 'Choose an address type'.
The address-type question is a GOV.UK radios group named addressType whose fieldset legend repeats 'Choose an address type' and is visually hidden.

The address-type page offers three options in this order: 'Origin or Consignor' with hint 'Place of origin, Consignor'; 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' with hint 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'; 'Transporter' with hint 'Private, Commercial'.
The address-type page has one button, 'Continue'.
The address-type page's Back link goes to the address book list at /address-book.

The address-type question is required: Continue with nothing chosen, or with a value that is not one of the three types, shows the error 'Select an address type' in the error summary and against the radios, with status 400.
Choosing 'Origin or Consignor' or 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and pressing Continue stores the chosen type and goes to the add page at /address-book/add.
Choosing 'Transporter' and pressing Continue goes to the transporter type page at /address-book/add/transporter with start=true, and the hand-over is logged.
claims.quote: 'Address type question handed over to the add-a-transporter pages'

claims.statement: When the user comes back to the address-type page during an add, the type they chose before is shown checked.
The address-type page and the add page are sent with Cache-Control: no-store, so the browser does not keep a copy of the form.
The add page is served at GET and POST /address-book/add.
The add page is marked at maturity 'exploring'.
The add page has two modes: the address-book mode, opened from the address book after the address-type step, and the role-handshake mode, opened by a notification journey with a handshake context.

In the address-book mode, opening or posting the add page with no chosen address type that the form serves (Origin or Consignor, or Destination, Consignee or Importer) redirects to the address-type page; a stored Transporter choice also redirects there. The redirect is logged.
claims.quote: 'No address type chosen that this form serves, sending the user to choose one'

claims.statement: The add page shows the caption 'Add new address' in English.
claims.note: The address-type page before it uses the caption 'Add a new address'; the Welsh add caption reuses the address-type caption 'Ychwanegu cyfeiriad newydd'.

claims.statement: The add page's heading and page title are 'Add address and contact details', and the browser title reads 'Add address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
In the address-book mode the add page's Back link goes to the address-type page.
In the role-handshake mode the add page's Back link goes to the journey's return URL.
In the role-handshake mode the add page shows the draft journey strip (the Draft status and the notification id) above the caption; the address-book mode shows no journey strip.
In the role-handshake mode the add form carries the journey type, notification id, fulfilment id and handshake token as hidden fields, so a post keeps the journey context.
claims.note: mechanism: hidden form fields holding the handshake context; the context itself is part 3's.

claims.statement: The add form groups its fields under two level-2 headings: 'Address' (name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode, country) and 'Contact details' (email address, phone number).

The add form asks its fields in this order: Name or organisation, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address, Phone number.

export const fieldLabelsInFormOrder = [
  fieldLabels.name,
  fieldLabels.addressLine1,
  fieldLabels.addressLine2,
  fieldLabels.townOrCity,
  fieldLabels.county,
  fieldLabels.postcode,
  fieldLabels.countryCode,
  fieldLabels.email,
  fieldLabels.phone
]

claims.statement: The name field is labelled 'Name or organisation', is full width, has no autocomplete attribute and has no hint.
The name is required and at most 255 characters.
A blank name shows 'Enter a name or organisation'; a name over 255 characters shows 'Name must be 255 characters or fewer'.
claims.quote:
required: 'Enter a name or organisation',
      maxLength: (max) => `Name must be ${max} characters or fewer`

claims.statement: Address line 1 is labelled 'Address line 1', is full width and has autocomplete 'address-line1'.
Address line 1 is required and at most 255 characters.
A blank address line 1 shows 'Enter address line 1'; one over 255 characters shows 'Address line 1 must be 255 characters or fewer'.
claims.quote:
required: 'Enter address line 1',
      maxLength: (max) => `Address line 1 must be ${max} characters or fewer`

claims.statement: Address line 2 is labelled 'Address line 2 (optional)', is full width and has autocomplete 'address-line2'.
Address line 2 is optional and at most 255 characters; over 255 shows 'Address line 2 must be 255 characters or fewer'.
Town or city is labelled 'Town or city', is one-half width and has autocomplete 'address-level2'.
Town or city is required and at most 100 characters.
A blank town or city shows 'Enter a town or city'; one over 100 characters shows 'Town or city must be 100 characters or fewer'.
claims.quote:
required: 'Enter a town or city',
      maxLength: (max) => `Town or city must be ${max} characters or fewer`

claims.statement: County is labelled 'County (optional)', is one-half width and has no autocomplete attribute.
County is optional and at most 100 characters; over 100 shows 'County must be 100 characters or fewer'.
Postcode is labelled 'Postcode or Zip code', is one-half width and has autocomplete 'postal-code'.
Postcode is required and at most 12 characters.
A blank postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code'; one over 12 characters shows 'Postcode must be 12 characters or fewer'.
claims.quote:
required: 'Enter a postcode or Zip code',
      maxLength: (max) => `Postcode must be ${max} characters or fewer`

claims.statement: The add form does not check a postcode's format: the field rules give postcode only required and a maximum length, and the UK postcode validator in lib/validate is not used, so any text up to 12 characters is accepted for any country.
claims.note: Follows from fieldRuleFor building only required/max-length text rules for fields without email or oneOfCountryCodes.

claims.statement: Country is a plain GOV.UK select labelled 'Country', one-half width, with no autocomplete attribute.
Country is required and must be one of the country codes the form offered; a blank or unoffered country shows 'Select a country'.
The country select's first option is the placeholder 'Select a country' with an empty value.
The country list comes from the reference-data service's countries endpoint, each option showing the country name with its code as the value.
The country list always includes United Kingdom (code GB), named 'United Kingdom' whatever reference data calls it, and lists it once.
claims.note: mechanism: drops any GB entry reference data returns and adds its own United Kingdom entry.

claims.statement: The country list is sorted alphabetically by name in English collation, United Kingdom among them rather than first.
When reference data returns no countries, or the countries request fails, the page fails with a service-unavailable error ('Reference data unavailable', dataset countries).
Countries are fetched from reference data once and then held in memory for the life of the service process; in stub mode the captured countries fixture is used instead and no request is made.
claims.note: mechanism: in-process cache of the countries list.

claims.statement: The countries request sends the trace id in the configured tracing header, and can ask for named country blocks as repeated 'blocks' query parameters; the add form asks for no blocks.
In the address-book mode the add form opens with United Kingdom selected in the country select.

In the role-handshake mode the add form opens with United Kingdom selected for a receiving party (such as the consignee) and with 'Select a country' for any other party (such as the consignor or place of origin).
Email address is labelled 'Email address', is full width and has autocomplete 'email'.
Email address is required, at most 254 characters, and must be in email format; any top-level domain is accepted.
claims.quote: email: { maxLength: 254, required: true, email: true }

claims.statement: A blank email shows 'Enter an email address'; a malformed one shows 'Enter an email address in the correct format'; one over 254 characters shows 'Email address must be 254 characters or fewer'.
claims.quote:
required: 'Enter an email address',
      format: 'Enter an email address in the correct format',
      maxLength: (max) => `Email address must be ${max} characters or fewer`

claims.statement: Phone number is labelled 'Phone number', is two-thirds width, has autocomplete 'tel' and the hint 'For international numbers include the country code'.
claims.quote: const PHONE_HINT = 'For international numbers include the country code'

claims.statement: Phone number is required and at most 20 characters.
A blank phone number shows 'Enter a phone number'; one over 20 characters shows 'Phone number must be 20 characters or fewer'.
claims.quote:
required: 'Enter a phone number',
      maxLength: (max) => `Phone number must be ${max} characters or fewer`

claims.statement: The add form does not check a phone number's format: the field rules give phone only required and a maximum length, and the UK phone validator in lib/validate is not used.
claims.note: Follows from fieldRuleFor building only required/max-length text rules for a field without the email flag.

claims.statement: Only Phone number has a hint; no other address or contact field shows a hint.
Every text field's value is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is checked and saved, so a value of only spaces counts as blank.
claims.note: mechanism: Joi convert mode returns the trimmed value, which is what the add page saves.

claims.statement: Validation checks every field at once and shows at most one error per field, the first that field fails.
When the add form is refused, the error summary lists each error as a link in field order, each field shows its error inline, the entered values are kept, and the response status is 400.
A user's own input errors on the add form are not logged.
claims.note: No logger call on the validation-refusal branch.

claims.statement: Selecting an error summary link moves focus to the field it names.
A refused add page has its page title prefixed 'Error: '.
In the address-book mode, after the address fields a visible section break precedes a roles question: GOV.UK checkboxes named roles, legend in medium size.
For an 'Origin or Consignor' address the roles question's legend is 'What can this address be used for?'.
claims.quote: ORIGIN_OR_CONSIGNOR: 'What can this address be used for?'

claims.statement: For a 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' address the roles question's legend is 'Address type'.
claims.note: The two address types use different legends for the same roles question.

claims.statement: In the address-book mode the roles question's hint is 'Select where this address can be used'.
claims.quote: hint: 'Select where this address can be used'

claims.statement: For an 'Origin or Consignor' address the roles offered are, in order, 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor'.
For a 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' address the roles offered are, in order, 'Place of destination', 'Consignee' and 'Importer': the place role comes first.
The role checkboxes have no hints and open unticked on a new add.
The role option labels are 'Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'.
claims.quote:
PLACE_OF_ORIGIN: { label: 'Place of origin' },
      CONSIGNOR: { label: 'Consignor' },
      CONSIGNEE: { label: 'Consignee' },
      IMPORTER: { label: 'Importer' },

claims.statement: In the address-book mode at least one role must be ticked; none shows 'Select what this address can be used for', and the summary link focuses the first role.
claims.quote: required: 'Select what this address can be used for'

claims.statement: The roles error is listed after the address and contact field errors in the summary.
Only roles the chosen address type offers are saved; any other posted role is dropped, and when one is dropped it is logged.
claims.quote: 'Posted roles the address page does not offer were not saved'
claims.note: mechanism: filters posted roles against the roles of the chosen type (address-book mode) or of the journey party (role-handshake mode).

claims.statement: In the role-handshake mode the roles question's legend is 'What else should this address be used for?'.
claims.quote: journeyLegend: 'What else should this address be used for?'

claims.statement: In the role-handshake mode the roles hint names the party the address is being added for, with 'a' or 'an' by its first letter: 'This address is being added as a <role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.'
claims.quote: `This address is being added as ${/^[AEIOU]/.test(roleLabel) ? 'an' : 'a'} ${roleLabel} address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.`
claims.note: The article test checks upper-case vowels only, while the role labels it receives ('Place of origin', 'Importer') start with a capital, so 'an Importer' reads correctly.

claims.statement: In the role-handshake mode the roles question offers only the other roles on the party's side, unticked: place of origin offers Consignor; consignor offers Place of origin; consignee offers Importer and Place of destination; importer offers Consignee and Place of destination; place of destination offers Consignee and Importer.
In the role-handshake mode the roles question is left out when the party has no other roles to offer.
In the role-handshake mode no role need be ticked: there is no roles error, and the address is saved with the party's own role plus any other roles ticked.
claims.note: That the party's own role is saved rests on rolesToSaveForParty (journey-registry.js, part 3) and the test that a consignee add with Importer ticked lists as 'Consignee, Importer'.

claims.statement: In the address-book mode the add page has one button, 'Save and continue'.
In the address-book mode the add page has a link 'Cancel and return to address book' to /address-book; following it creates no address.
claims.quote: const CANCEL_AND_RETURN_TO_ADDRESS_BOOK = 'Cancel and return to address book'

claims.statement: In the role-handshake mode the add page has two buttons, 'Save and select' (primary) and 'Save and return to address page' (secondary), and a link 'Cancel and return to hub'.
claims.quote:
saveAndSelect: 'Save and select',
    saveAndReturnToAddressPage: 'Save and return to address page',

claims.statement: In the role-handshake mode the 'Cancel and return to hub' link goes to the journey's return URL with the cancel landing, and following it creates no address.
A post to the add page carrying a cancel field redirects to the cancel destination of its mode without saving; in the role-handshake mode the cancel is logged.
claims.note: The template renders Cancel as a link, not a button, so this branch is reached only by a post that sends cancel.

claims.statement: A valid add saves a new address to the address-book service for the signed-in organisation, holding name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, country code, email, phone and the roles kept.

After a valid add in the address-book mode, the add in progress is cleared, the success banner '<name> address added to your address book' is set, and the user lands on page 1 of the address book list on the tab of the chosen address type.
claims.quote: added: (name) => `${name} address added to your address book`
claims.note: The success is logged with the organisation id, address id and address type.

claims.statement: After a valid add in the role-handshake mode, the browser is sent to the journey's return URL carrying the new address id and the landing the user chose: select for 'Save and select', return for 'Save and return to address page'.
claims.note: The hand-back is logged with the organisation id, journey type, notification id, fulfilment id, address id and landing.

claims.statement: When the address-book service refuses the new address as invalid, the add page shows the service's errors against the form fields with status 400, keeping the entered values, and the refusal is logged at warn.
claims.quote: logger.warn({ err, ...logContext }, 'Address book refused the new address')

claims.statement: When saving the new address fails for any other reason, the add page is shown again with a recoverable-error message and status 500, keeping the entered values, and the failure is logged at error.
claims.note: An HTTP error already raised as a Boom error (such as reference data unavailable) is passed on instead of re-rendering.

claims.statement: In the address-book mode the values entered and the roles ticked are kept for the add in progress on every post, so after a refused save the user can go Back to the address-type page, choose the same type again and see the address, contact details and ticked role they entered.
claims.note: mechanism: session record 'addressBookAddInProgress' holding the chosen type, the entered form values and the ticked roles.

claims.statement: The role-handshake mode keeps nothing in the add in progress: the form opens empty each time the journey opens it.
A stored address type that is not one of the three address types is ignored, as though no type were chosen.
claims.note: mechanism: guards the session record of the chosen address type.

claims.statement: A saved address shows in the address book list with each stored postal line on its own line, every line but the last ending in a comma, and its country in a separate column.
claims.note: mechanism: escapes each postal line (address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, blank lines dropped) and joins them with a line break and an optional line ending.

claims.statement: A saved address's country is shown by its name from the country list, and by its code when the code is not in the list.
claims.note: mechanism: country label lookup shared with the view and list pages.

claims.statement: A search term matches a country when the country's name contains the term, ignoring case and surrounding spaces; a blank term matches no country.
claims.note: mechanism: maps a free-text search to country codes; the list search is part 4's.

claims.statement: On an edit form the country select leaves out the 'Select a country' placeholder when the saved country is in the list, and shows it when it is not.
claims.note: Read in this part's country file; the edit page itself is part 6's.

claims.statement: A saved address or other record that is marked deleted, or that the service answers not found, is treated as not there.
claims.note: mechanism: live-record lookup used by the view, edit and delete pages (part 6). Any other lookup failure becomes an internal error after it is logged by the caller.

claims.statement: The address-book copy has a Welsh version of every add, address-type, field and error string; the Welsh file is marked as a machine draft, not reviewed by a translator, not to ship to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

lib/validate's requiredText makes a field required after trimming, with one message for blank or missing.

claims.statement: lib/validate's maxText and requiredMaxText cap a trimmed text field at a maximum length, optional or required, falling back to a shared default length message when none is given.
